problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $A(7,-2,3)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨9,2,1⟩+s⟨2,-2,1⟩$ and $r=⟨4,-5,19⟩+t⟨3,4,7⟩.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Parametric Equations of a Plane

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Parallel To Two Lines
examples.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $C(2,50,-19)$ and is parallel to the lines $\mathbf{r}= \langle 2,\sqrt{6},17 \rangle + s \langle -1,7,2 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{r}= \langle 20,-44, 27 \rangle + t \langle 2\sqrt{3},9,-8 \rangle$.
examples.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are $\mathbf{v_1}=\langle  -1,7,2  \rangle$ and $\mathbf{v_2}=\langle 2\sqrt{3},9,-8 \rangle$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $C(2,50,-19)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $\mathbf{c}=\langle 2,50,-19 \rangle.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =c+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨2,50,-19⟩+s\,⟨-1,7,2⟩+t\,⟨2\sqrt{3},9,-8⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=⟨1,7,-2⟩+t⟨-3,4,1⟩+s⟨5,1,-2⟩,\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨-3,4,1⟩$ and $w=⟨5,1,-2⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 4 & 1 \\ 5 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-9i-j-23k \\  & =⟨-9,-1,-23⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-9,-1,-23⟩.$
